scope: Studio release objects only; existing unrelated project advisories are outside this receipt.

findings.name: rls_enabled_no_policy
findings.title: RLS Enabled No Policy
findings.description: Detects cases where row level security (RLS) has been enabled on a table but no RLS policies have been created.

findings.detail: Table \`public.studio_creative_results\` has RLS enabled, but no policies exist
Table \`public.voice_storage_reservations\` has RLS enabled, but no policies exist

findings.name: authenticated_security_definer_function_executable
findings.title: Signed-In Users Can Execute SECURITY DEFINER Function
findings.description: Detects `SECURITY DEFINER` functions that are callable by signed-in users. Revoke `EXECUTE`, switch the function to `SECURITY INVOKER`, or move it out of your exposed API schema if signed-in users should not call it.

findings.detail: Function `public.studio_named_account_active()` can be executed by the `authenticated` role as a `SECURITY DEFINER` function via `/rest/v1/rpc/studio_named_account_active`. Revoke `EXECUTE` or switch it to `SECURITY INVOKER` if that is not intentional.

review: studio_creative_results and voice_storage_reservations intentionally have no client RLS policies. They are private server metadata, and all client/direct reservation writes are revoked.

studio_named_account_active is intentionally SECURITY DEFINER because the invoker gallery transaction must check the caller's current auth.users and deletion state. It takes no inputs, returns only a boolean for auth.uid(), sets an empty search_path, has no writes, and is executable only by authenticated callers. All gallery writes remain SECURITY INVOKER under RLS and named editor membership checks.

16 actual PostgreSQL gallery groups verify role, anonymous, deleting-account, wrong-listing and stale-snapshot rejection. 20 cleanup checks verify reservation grants, fixed deadlines and retained deletion inventory.
